newsitem.title: UK: UK's SFA expels two directors for deception.
newsitem.headline: UK's SFA expels two directors for deception.

text.p: The Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) said on Tuesday it had expelled two directors of Manchester-based stockbroking firm John Siddall & Son Ltd.

The British financial watchdog said Stephen Alexander and Gregory Banks had been expelled from the Register of Directors for deceiving it over matters concerning dealings for a client in Anglia Television Group shares in 1994.
Banks was fined 3,000 stg and told to pay costs of 9,190 stg, while Alexander is required to pay costs of 3,000 stg.
John Siddall & Son has been severely reprimanded.
In January 1994, one of Banks' clients, a Jersey company called Market Hill, made a profit of about 6,000 stg on a deal in Anglia Television shares.

When Siddall was told the Department of Trade and Industry inspectors would be investigating the dealings, its compliance officer was told by Banks that the beneficial owner of Market Hill was a Jersey-based individual.
In fact, Banks was the beneficial owner, the SFA said in the statement. Alexander supported Banks assertions, even though he knew them to be false, it added.
Alexander has accepted that, as senior executive officer at the time, he had prime responsibility for ensuring Siddall's compliance with SFA rules.
Siddall has a new controller and senior executive officer and has improved its compliance procedures.
United News & Media Plc now owns Anglia Television.
